harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (RHEL 7.9): SSH allowed from any address, TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 (10.100.8.11), and TCP/9000 rejected from node3 (10.100.8.12) and everywhere else. Verified behavior with live traffic, then restarted all three managed nodes one at a time, confirming boot-identity changes and post-reboot recovery of the firewall config and correct traffic behavior on each.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/firewalld state: RHEL 7.9, firewalld active, default zone 'public', ssh service already allowed
Added permanent firewalld rich rules on node1: accept TCP/9000 from 10.100.8.11 (node2); reject TCP/9000 from 10.100.8.12 (node3)

Discovered a RHEL7 firewalld ordering quirk (deny chain runs before allow chain within a zone) that caused an explicit generic 'reject 9000 from anywhere' rule to also block node2; removed that generic rule and relied on the zone's default catch-all REJECT for all other unmatched sources on port 9000
Reloaded firewalld and inspected the resulting iptables IN_public_allow/IN_public_deny chains to confirm correct rule placement
Started a temporary Python HTTP listener on node1:9000 and validated live traffic: node2 -> HTTP 200 (allowed), node3 -> connection refused (rejected), SSH reachable from both node2 and node3
Confirmed firewalld is systemctl-enabled for boot persistence, in addition to --permanent rule storage
Captured boot_id baseline on node1, node2, node3

Restarted node1 via 'sudo systemctl reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, re-verified firewalld rules persisted and port 9000 / SSH behavior unchanged after reboot with live traffic tests
Restarted node2, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed sshd active, re-verified node2's allowed access to node1:9000 still worked
Restarted node3, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed sshd active, re-verified node3 was still correctly rejected on port 9000 while SSH remained reachable
Cleaned up temporary test listener and files on node1

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: firewalld public zone has services=ssh with no source restriction; node3 (an unrelated address) successfully opened TCP/22 to node1
Permanent rich-rule accept for 10.100.8.11 added; live curl from node2 to node1:9000 returned HTTP 200 both before and after node2's reboot

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
evidence.summary: Explicit reject rule for 10.100.8.12 plus zone default REJECT for all other sources; live curl from node3 to node1:9000 was refused (curl exit 7) both before and after node3's reboot, with iptables counters confirming the REJECT rule was hit
node1 boot_id changed from ef457a88... to 918095e7... after 'systemctl reboot'; post-reboot firewall-cmd --list-all shows the same accept/reject rich rules still present and firewalld active/enabled

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence (baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ef457a88...; reboot acknowledged (connection closed); post-reboot boot_id 918095e7... (changed); firewalld config and live port 9000/SSH behavior confirmed recovered via node2/node3 traffic tests

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence (baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 73bafeef...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 2c0ea2bf... (changed); sshd active and node2's HTTP request to node1:9000 succeeded post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence (baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 192f6cab...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 5ddbf0f3... (changed); sshd active, and node3 was still correctly rejected on port 9000 (curl exit 7) while SSH remained reachable post-reboot
